title: Hubble views NGC 4522
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 4522, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 4522 · constellation Virgo · about 60 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Though this is a still image, the spiral galaxy NGC 4522 almost seems to swirl, with ghostly gas being driven out of it. Bright blue pockets of newborn stars sit to the right and left of centre. The galaxy lies some 60 million light-years away, in the Virgo galaxy cluster.

NGC 4522 is being stripped of its gas right now. It races through the cluster so fast, an estimated 10 million kilometres per hour or more, that it meets a strong wind from the thin, hot gas that fills the cluster. That wind pushes the galaxy's own gas out behind it, a process called ram pressure stripping.

The effect is powerful enough to mangle galaxies and even shut down their star formation, since gas is the fuel stars are made from. Oddly, some of the stripped gas has formed new star clusters of its own, and several of them are visible in this Hubble picture.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.06 x 3.06 arcminutes) and distance (60 million light years), the frame spans roughly 53,000 × 53,000 light-years. Its light set out about 60 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, using blue, visible and near-infrared filters. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The faint streams of stripped gas are far too dim for the eye and only show up in Hubble's long exposures.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys gives astronomers a detailed view of ram pressure stripping in action, including the newly formed star clusters that developed in the gas torn from the galaxy.
alt: A spiral galaxy with wispy gas being forced out of it and bright blue patches of new stars to the right and left of centre.
